answer: Transitive trust graphs curb Sybil attacks by bounding agent interactions along certified peer attestations. Nodes log mutual endorsements in a credential vault, deploying an audit lantern to detect sparse topological cuts. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring authentic trust edges from honest nodes per identity, dampening any gale of automated clones. However, this reliance on social capital penalizes legitimate new entrants who lack established network ties.
